title: Roasted Red Pepper Soup
subtitle: Silky, smoky soup made from oven-roasted peppers and tomatoes
excerpt: Roasting concentrates the sweetness of red peppers and gives this soup a deep, smoky flavour. It takes very little effort: everything goes in the roasting tin together, then blends smooth.
sourceNotes: Roasted pepper soups are popular across the Mediterranean. This version draws on Spanish and Italian traditions of charring peppers as a base for sauces and soups.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and reheat gently, adding a splash of stock if needed.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a large roasting tin so the vegetables are not crowded.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 3 days ahead. The flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: Let the vegetables char at the edges in the oven. Those dark patches are where the flavour lives, not a sign that anything has gone wrong.
Preheat the oven. Put the peppers, onion, garlic, and cherry tomatoes in the roasting tin. Drizzle with olive oil and season well. Scatter the thyme sprigs over.
Roast for 40 to 45 minutes until the peppers are soft and beginning to char at the edges. The tomatoes will burst and the garlic will be completely soft.
Remove the thyme sprigs. Squeeze the roasted garlic from its skins into the tin.
Transfer everything to the blender jug. Add the smoked paprika and 300ml of the stock. Blend until very smooth.
Pour the blended soup into a saucepan. Add the remaining stock to reach your desired consistency. Heat through, season, and serve.

items.symptom: The soup has a bitter aftertaste.
items.cause: The peppers or garlic scorched too far beyond light charring.
items.fix: Remove any very dark pieces before blending.

items.symptom: The soup is grainy rather than silky.
items.cause: The blender did not run long enough.
items.fix: Blend for a full 2 minutes; pass through a sieve for extra smoothness.

items.cause: Not enough stock was added before serving.
items.fix: Stir in extra hot stock until you reach the right consistency.
